findings.element: .b-behindDate — the date lane in "How you got here" (day), "Behind you" (desk, owner) and the same block on the printed sheet
findings.problem: The lane is a hard 76px and the string is 11px Geist Mono, uppercase, at 0.16em: 6.6px advance plus 1.76px tracking is 8.36px a character, so any ten-character date needs about 84px and breaks. Driven with the disclosure opened at 390, 768, 1280 and 1440, the wedding-morning record renders four of its eight moments as SAT / 18 APR, SAT / 22 AUG, SAT / 29 AUG, SAT / 19 SEP while SAT 1 AUG and FRI 2 JAN stay whole — measured heights 35px against 18px in the same column. Every date with a two-digit day breaks, which is two thirds of a calendar, and the weekday is severed from the day it belongs to. The rows then inherit the damage: row heights alternate 39px and 55px, so the one place a guest reads the story of the year has a ragged left column and no vertical rhythm. Nothing in the shot set shows it because the disclosure is closed by default and the closed panel clips the overflowing lines; the brief forces it open in the record room and in print, which is exactly where the defect lives. The audit's tracking ladder cannot see it — the letterfit is correct, the lane is simply too narrow for the letterfit.
findings.fix: In b.css change .b-behindDate from width: 76px; line-height: 1.6 to width: 96px; line-height: 1.5; white-space: nowrap. 96px clears the longest string this format can produce (SAT 22 AUG at 10 characters is 84px, and a THU 30 SEPT at 11 is 92px), the nowrap makes a future overrun visible as a lane collision the gate can assert rather than a silent break, and 1.5 puts the 11px mono step back on the same leading as .b-date. The 20px comes out of the title lane, which has it: measured 344px on the day card and 316px on the sheet, against a longest fixture title of 190px. Then add to interaction-check.mjs, with the disclosure opened at 390 and 1440: assert every .b-behindDate box height equals its single-line height.

findings.problem: On the printed sheet the moment titles get a 192px lane at 17px Geist, about 21 characters, so Menu tasting at The Orchard and Choose the evening music each break to two lines while the 300px column beside them is empty for 600px below the count. Measured at 1440: .b-two is 300px + 48px + 316px inside a 794px sheet, and the rows column spends 124px of its 316 on the number lane before the person's words start. Worse, the two-column rule that creates that lane lives in @media (min-width: 1280px), so the paper's layout is decided by the browser window rather than by the paper: the same A4 page composed at 1024 gives those titles 540px and sets every one of them on a single line. A keepsake is the one artifact that cannot reflow after it is made, and this one has two different measures depending on which screen made it. I applied the fix below in the live page and re-measured: 192px becomes 292px and all seven fixture titles set on one line.
findings.fix: Three edits in b.css. (1) Give the paper its own layout trigger instead of the window's: add container-type: inline-size to .tl-stage, move the [data-medium="sheet"] .b-two rule out of @media (min-width: 1280px) into @container (min-width: 700px), and leave the [data-medium="full"] rules in the viewport query where they belong. (2) In that rule set grid-template-columns: 300px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 32px. (3) Narrow the sheet's own margins and number lane: [data-medium="sheet"] .b-print { padding: 56px 36px 44px }, and in the min-width: 701px block change the sheet's .b-measure padding-left to 96px, .b-item and .b-origin left to 96px, .b-away to left: -96px; width: 64px, .b-rail to left: 72px and the sheet tick offsets from -27px to -23px. No font-size, tracking or leading changes, so the ramp and the tracking gate are untouched.

findings.element: .b-dayCount — the word "Today" on the wedding morning
findings.problem: Putting the word in the count's slot is right; inheriting the count's face is not. .b-dayCount is Geist Mono at 96px with letter-spacing: var(--track-display), a step tuned for tabular figures, and the word pays for both decisions. In a monospaced face the T sits in the same 57.6px advance as the d, so the word opens with a visible hole between T and "oday" while -4.32px crushes o–d and a–y: the colour of the single most emotional word in the product is uneven, and it reads as a terminal string. It is also the widest thing on the card — 266px of ink inside a 300px content box, 17px of air each side. Every other word in the artifact is Geist; only figures are mono, and the file states that rule for the unfurl card in its own comment ("as a second uppercase mono stamp the couple's own date read as a machine label") and then breaks it here at 96px. The behaviour gate asserts the word is "Today" and that its size holds the count's register; neither assertion touches the family, so the gate stays green either way.
findings.fix: In b.css set .b-dayCount { font-family: var(--sans); font-weight: 600; font-size: 96px; line-height: 0.9; letter-spacing: var(--track-display); } and leave .b-num and .b-ogNum in mono, so the rule becomes the one the rest of the file already keeps: figures are mono, words are sans. Measured with the change applied: ink drops from 266px to 250px, giving 25px of air each side on a 390px phone, and the T–o hole closes. No new size, no new weight, no new tracking step, and Geist at 96px is a family the ladder already binds to --track-display, so the audit's one-letterfit-per-family-per-size rule still passes. If the count and the word must share a weight, 400 also works at 236px of ink; 600 is the one that carries the morning.

findings.problem: The tracking ladder was built because a value set per component drifted into five settings for one size, and it now holds — six steps, size-bound, enforced. Leading is the same axis and got none of that. Measured across 11 states and 4 widths, the master renders 13 distinct line-height ratios, and the same size carries several: 15px sans runs at 1.35, 1.40, 1.45, 1.50 and 1.60; 17px sans at 1.30, 1.50 and 1.55; 13px sans at 1.50 and 1.55; 20px sans at 1.30 and 1.40; 30px sans at 1.12 and 1.30; 11px mono at 1.20, 1.40 and 1.50; and the 96px count itself at 0.86 in the countdown and 0.90 on the morning, so the display object changes its own baseline between the two screens it exists on. It shows within a single screen, not only across the set: the wedding-morning card sets 15px prose at 1.60 (.b-dayNote) above 15px prose at 1.50 (.b-behindTitle), and 11px mono at 1.60 (.b-behindDate) beside 11px mono at 1.50 (.b-date). The audit checks that leading is declared and above its floor, which is why none of this is visible to it.
findings.fix: Add a leading ladder to shell.css beside the tracking one and bind it the same way: --lead-display: 0.9 (96 and 148), --lead-title: 1.05 (48 and 64), --lead-head: 1.2 (24, 30, 38), --lead-date: 1.3 (the 20px ceremonial line), --lead-body: 1.5 (13, 15, 17 prose), --lead-label: 1.4 (11 and 12 mono labels and single-line controls). Then replace every hand-set line-height in b.css with the step its size is on — .b-num 0.86 to var(--lead-display), .b-dayNote 1.6 to var(--lead-body), .b-note and .b-endedBody and .b-pressBody 1.55 to var(--lead-body), .b-bubble 1.45 and .b-unfurlTitle 1.35 to var(--lead-body), .b-behindDate 1.6 to var(--lead-label), .b-dayDate 1.4 and .b-when 1.3 to var(--lead-date), .b-endedTitle 1.12 to var(--lead-head) — and extend audit.mjs with the same assertion it already runs on tracking: fail when one family at one size renders at two leadings anywhere in the state matrix.

findings.element: .b-sub ("Wedding day at The Orchard") against .b-gapNote ("Nothing is planned until 1 August.") on the guest and owner horizon
findings.problem: On the surface a guest opens on a phone, the two sentences under the count are the couple's own description of their day and the system's report about an empty stretch of calendar, and they are set identically: Geist 15px, weight 400, --track-body, 1.5, fore-62, 40px apart, both ranged left on the same edge. Nothing tells a reader which of them a person wrote. The library's rule is that a person's words take the larger, denser type wherever they sit beside the machine's, and this artifact spends its entire scale on that principle everywhere else — the row title outranks its mono date, the unfurl card was rebuilt to stop stamping the couple's date as a label. The horizon is the one place it lapses, and it is the first block on every guest screen: phone, desk, print and the owner flight all carry the pair.
findings.fix: In b.css raise the owner-written line and leave the machine's where it is: .b-sub { font-size: 17px; line-height: var(--lead-body); letter-spacing: var(--track-body); color: var(--fore-72); } — 17px, 0.72 and --track-body are all declared steps, so nothing new enters the ramp, and .b-gapNote stays at 15px/fore-62. At sheet and full width, where .b-when already rises from 20px to 30px, add [data-medium="sheet"] .b-sub, [data-medium="full"] .b-sub { font-size: 20px; letter-spacing: var(--track-body); } to the min-width: 701px block so the pair keeps the same two-step separation on the desk and on paper.

biggestWin: The tracking ladder is now real. Round 2 found one size rendering at two letterfits in eight places and eight prose blocks with no tracking at all; driven across 11 states and 4 widths, this master renders 24 distinct type settings and every family-plus-size pair now has exactly one letterfit, with the audit failing the build if that ever stops being true — a declared ladder that is mechanically enforced is rarer in shipped software than it sounds, and it is the reason a three-colour, two-weight system still produces hierarchy a stranger can read on a phone. Under it: 96 and 148px tabular mono figures hung to the column with a hand-measured optical inset, so the countdown never twitches as it counts; a 24px sans title carrying the person's words above an 11px mono date, so the human string always outranks the machine string; word-safe clamping that keeps the whole sentence in the accessible name and re-runs on fonts.ready and resize; measures declared in ch on every prose block, including the two that were missing last round; and one uppercase-mono micro-label register that is not allowed to set a sentence. What stands between this and 9.5 is not a different decision and not a rebuild — it is one face swap on the morning word, one lane widened in the record room, one A4 layout that stops asking the browser window how wide the paper is, and the leading ladder that tracking already proved this file knows how to build. Call it a day of work, all of it inside the palette, the two weights and the architecture as locked.
